findings.reason: the plan's "missing third member" framing is wrong; it is a generalisation of a mechanism that exists, and the plan should say so and reuse it.
findings.text: the existing `grammar_content_digest()` already digests authority source canonically with an mtime-signature cache, and `imas_codex/cli/sn.py:1315` `_auto_sync_grammar()` already compares the installed digest against a stored `ISNGrammarVersion.content_digest` at startup; the plan proposes the same mechanism and cites neither.

findings.reason: two parallel authority-digest implementations drift; the honest change is to factor `grammar_sync.py`'s hasher into a shared helper and register the schema alongside DD/grammar.
findings.text: the plan adds a second digest/store/compare/refuse path beside the owner (`grammar_content_digest` + `_finalise_active_version` + `_auto_sync_grammar` at `imas_codex/cli/sn.py:1315`) instead of extracting the shared helper and extending it to the LinkML schema authority.

findings.reason: naming the extension point converts a new subsystem into a small addition to an existing owner.
findings.text: the design's digest function and connect-time comparison are a thin layer over the existing synchronizer, and the plan does not justify why `GraphSchema` (the declared "single source of truth for the graph structure") and the `gen_schema_context.py` source list cannot be extended to emit the digest.

findings.reason: the plan should name one owner (e.g. a shared authority-digest helper under `imas_codex/graph/`) that all three call, rather than leaving the surface undefined.
findings.text: no module is named to own the digest; it must be emitted by the generator that already enumerates the schema sources, stored via the grammar-sync finalise path, and read by `AgentsServer.__post_init__` (`imas_codex/llm/server.py:1830`), so the one concept is split across three call sites.

findings.reason: the section must account for the interface surface it adds, and here the surface is reducible to a field/registration on an existing authority node.
findings.text: §5 adds a new node type and a new refusal family without stating what they merge with or retire; the node shape it describes is already `ISNGrammarVersion.content_digest` (same field semantics) and the refusal extends the existing fail-closed synchronizer behaviour.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the design distributes one concept (canonicalise→hash→store→compare→refuse) across schema generation, a node write, and a server connect check with no named owner, while the schema owner `imas_codex/graph/schema.py` (`GraphSchema`, "single source of truth for the graph structure") is never cited.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the digest-and-reconcile-at-startup mechanism already has an owner to extend, `imas_codex/standard_names/grammar_sync.py:144`, with its startup driver in `imas_codex/cli/sn.py:1315`; the plan proposes a second mechanism beside it.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §5 adds a new graph node type and a new refusal family (server refuses to serve on mismatch) without naming what either merges with or retires, or stating why nothing can be — the node shape it describes already exists as `ISNGrammarVersion.content_digest` and the refusal could extend that family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan asserts the LinkML schema has "no such node and no digest anywhere" and cites only the passive `DDVersion`, missing the existing digest-source-and-compare-at-startup mechanism in `imas_codex/standard_names/grammar_sync.py:144` (`grammar_content_digest`) + `imas_codex/cli/sn.py:1315` (`_auto_sync_grammar`) and the source enumeration already in `scripts/gen_schema_context.py:47`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the proposed schema digest function and startup comparison are a parallel thin re-implementation of `grammar_content_digest()` and the `_auto_sync_grammar()` synchronizer; the plan does not say why those cannot be generalised.
